grammar.title: Advanced relative clauses
grammar.explanation_pt:
**1. Preposição + which / whom (formal)**
Na fala, a preposição vai para o final; em textos formais, ela vem **antes** do pronome:
- Informal: "the city (that) I grew up **in**"
- Formal: "the city **in which** I grew up"
- Informal: "the people I work **with**" → Formal: "the people **with whom** I work"
⚠️ Depois de preposição, use **which** (coisas) ou **whom** (pessoas) — **nunca** that ou who: ❌ "in that", ❌ "with who".

**2. Which para comentar a frase inteira** (= o que)
- "Rents have doubled, **which** means many families have had to move."
- "He didn't apologize, **which** I found rude."
Sempre com **vírgula** e sempre **which** (nunca that, nunca what): ❌ "..., what is a problem".

**3. Quantificador + of which / of whom**
**some / many / most / all / none / both / neither / half / one / a few + of which (coisas) / of whom (pessoas)**
- "The city has 30 parks, **most of which** are in rich areas."
- "I have two brothers, **both of whom** live abroad."
- "We received 200 complaints, **none of which** were answered."

**4. Whose** (posse — pessoas **e** coisas)
- "a neighbourhood **whose** residents are fighting gentrification"
- Formal: "the building, the roof **of which** collapsed" (= whose roof)

**5. Where / when / why** em vez de preposição + which:
- "the area **where** I live" (= in which) · "the year **when** the metro opened" · "the reason **why** I left"

**Lembrete:** relative clause **não restritiva** (informação extra) vem entre vírgulas e **não aceita that**.

dialogue.title: Should we move?
dialogue.context_pt: Um casal discute se deve se mudar do centro para a periferia da cidade.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.en: Our rent's going up again in January — by fifteen percent, which is ridiculous.
lines.pt: Nosso aluguel vai subir de novo em janeiro — quinze por cento, o que é ridículo.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.en: I know. Maybe it's time to look at the neighbourhood where my sister lives. It's much cheaper.
lines.pt: Eu sei. Talvez seja hora de olhar o bairro onde minha irmã mora. É bem mais barato.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.en: But it's on the outskirts. I'd be commuting for two hours a day, most of which I'd spend standing on a crowded train.
lines.pt: Mas é na periferia. Eu ficaria duas horas por dia no trajeto, a maior parte das quais em pé num trem lotado.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.en: True. Although the new metro line, which opens next year, will stop right there.
lines.pt: Verdade. Mas a nova linha de metrô, que abre ano que vem, vai parar bem lá.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.en: "Next year" — that's what they said three years ago. And what about our friends, most of whom live around here?
lines.pt: "Ano que vem" — foi o que disseram há três anos. E os nossos amigos, que em sua maioria moram por aqui?

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.en: We'd see them at weekends. And we'd have a garden, which we've always wanted.
lines.pt: A gente veria eles nos fins de semana. E teríamos um quintal, o que sempre quisemos.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.en: That's a good point. OK, let's visit a few places this weekend — but only ones from which I can walk to a station.
lines.pt: Bom argumento. OK, vamos visitar alguns lugares neste fim de semana — mas só os que dão para ir a pé até uma estação.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.en: Deal.
lines.pt: Combinado.

listening.title: Open streets
listening.context_pt: Uma reportagem de rádio sobre ruas fechadas para carros aos domingos.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.en: It's Sunday morning on one of the busiest avenues in the city — except that today, there isn't a single car. Since the avenue started closing to traffic on Sundays, it has become a huge open-air park, which attracts thousands of cyclists, skaters, families and street musicians. Bogotá, in Colombia, is often cited as the pioneer of this idea: its weekly Ciclovía, which began in the 1970s, now opens many kilometres of roads to people instead of cars. Not everyone is happy, of course. Some shop owners, most of whom depend on drivers, complain that they lose customers. But surveys in several cities suggest that most residents support the idea, many of whom say it's the only time they feel the city really belongs to them.

questions.q: What happens to the avenue on Sundays?
questions.answer: It closes to cars and becomes an open-air park.

questions.q: Which city is cited as the pioneer?
questions.answer: Bogotá, with its Ciclovía (since the 1970s).

questions.q: Who complains, and why?
questions.answer: Some shop owners, because they depend on drivers and lose customers.

questions.q: What do many residents say?
questions.answer: It's the only time they feel the city belongs to them.

reading.title: The 15-minute city
reading.text: Imagine a neighbourhood in which you could reach almost everything you need — work, school, shops, a doctor, a park — within a 15-minute walk or bike ride. This is the idea behind the "15-minute city", a concept popularized by the urbanist Carlos Moreno, whose work influenced the plans of Paris mayor Anne Hidalgo. Supporters argue that cities designed around cars have created long commutes, pollution and lonely suburbs, all of which damage our health and quality of life. By bringing services closer to people, the 15-minute city aims to cut emissions, revive local businesses and give residents more free time. Several cities, among which are Melbourne, Barcelona and Bogotá, have experimented with similar ideas. The concept is not without its critics, however. Some point out that in many cities, including those in Brazil, jobs and good services are concentrated in a few central areas, which means that a 15-minute city could easily become a privilege for the rich. Others fear that improving a neighbourhood will push up rents, forcing out the very people for whom the changes were intended. The challenge, then, is not only to design better neighbourhoods, but to ensure that everyone can afford to live in them.

questions.q: What is a 15-minute city?
questions.answer: A neighbourhood where you can reach most things you need within a 15-minute walk or bike ride.

questions.q: What problems do supporters say car-based cities have created?
questions.answer: Long commutes, pollution and lonely suburbs.

questions.q: Why could it become a privilege for the rich in Brazil?
questions.answer: Jobs and good services are concentrated in a few central areas.

questions.q: What risk do others fear?
questions.answer: Rising rents could force out the people the changes were meant to help.

writing.task: Write a proposal to your city council (220–260 words) suggesting one improvement for your neighbourhood. Describe the current situation, your proposal and its benefits. Use at least 6 advanced relative clauses (preposition + which/whom, which for a whole clause, quantifier + of which/whom, whose).
writing.task_pt: Escreva uma proposta para a câmara municipal (220–260 palavras) sugerindo uma melhoria para o seu bairro. Descreva a situação atual, sua proposta e os benefícios. Use pelo menos 6 relative clauses avançadas.
writing.model:
Proposal: Turning the old market square into a community park

Introduction
The purpose of this proposal is to suggest a new use for the old market square in Jardim Esperança, a neighbourhood in which more than 40,000 people live but where there is not a single public park.

The current situation
The square, whose market closed in 2018, is now used as an informal car park. It is poorly lit, which makes many residents, especially women and older people, feel unsafe at night. Local children, most of whom live in small flats, have nowhere safe to play.

The proposal
We propose transforming the square into a small park with trees, a playground, benches and an outdoor gym. A local architect, with whom our residents' association has already spoken, has offered to design the project at no cost. The area could also host a weekly farmers' market, the profits from which would help pay for maintenance.

Benefits
The park would provide a green space for thousands of families, many of whom cannot afford to travel to the large parks in the city centre. It would also improve safety and support local producers. Studies in several cities have found that access to green spaces is associated with better physical and mental health.

Conclusion
We strongly believe that this project, the costs of which are relatively low, would make a real difference to our community. We would be happy to present our ideas at the next council meeting.

grammar.title: Participle clauses
grammar.explanation_pt:
Participle clauses **encurtam** orações quando o **sujeito é o mesmo**. Há três formas:

**1. Present participle (-ing)** → sentido **ativo** / ações simultâneas
- Relative clause reduzida: "People **who live** in cities..." → "People **living** in cities..."
- Tempo: "**While I was walking** home, I saw..." → "**Walking** home, I saw..."
- Causa: "**Because I didn't know** the answer, I stayed quiet." → "**Not knowing** the answer, I stayed quiet."
- Resultado: "The storm hit the coast, **causing** serious damage."

**2. Past participle (-ed / 3ª forma)** → sentido **passivo**
- "The houses **which were built** in the 1950s..." → "The houses **built** in the 1950s..."
- "**Built** in 1960, Brasília was designed by Lúcio Costa and Oscar Niemeyer."
- "**Asked** about the problem, the mayor refused to comment."

**3. Perfect participle (having + particípio)** → ação **anterior** à principal
- "**After she had finished** university, she moved to Lisbon." → "**Having finished** university, she moved to Lisbon."
- Passiva: "**Having been** rejected twice, he finally got the job."

**Negativa:** **not** antes do particípio: "**Not having** a car, I take the bus."

⚠️ **Dangling participle (erro clássico):** o sujeito da participle clause **tem que ser** o mesmo da oração principal.
❌ "**Walking** down the street, the rain started." (a chuva estava andando?)
✅ "**Walking** down the street, **I** got caught in the rain."

Not knowing the way, we got lost.

grammar.tip_pt: "**Having said that**" é uma expressão fixa muito usada para introduzir um contraste depois de concordar com algo: "Remote work has many benefits. **Having said that**, it can be very lonely."

dialogue.title: Then and now
dialogue.context_pt: Uma jornalista entrevista um senhor de 85 anos sobre as mudanças que ele viu na vida.

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.en: Seu Antônio, having lived for 85 years, you've seen enormous changes. What's the biggest one?
lines.pt: Seu Antônio, tendo vivido 85 anos, o senhor viu mudanças enormes. Qual é a maior?

lines.speaker: Seu Antônio
lines.en: Probably the move to the cities. Born on a farm in Minas, I came to São Paulo at seventeen, carrying one suitcase.
lines.pt: Provavelmente a mudança para as cidades. Nascido numa fazenda em Minas, vim para São Paulo aos dezessete, carregando uma mala.

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.en: What was it like?
lines.pt: Como foi?

lines.speaker: Seu Antônio
lines.en: Hard. Not knowing anyone, I slept at a cousin's house for months. Having worked on the farm since I was a child, I was used to hard work, though.
lines.pt: Difícil. Sem conhecer ninguém, dormi na casa de um primo por meses. Mas, tendo trabalhado na fazenda desde criança, eu estava acostumado com trabalho pesado.

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.en: And today? What do you think of young people's lives?
lines.pt: E hoje? O que o senhor acha da vida dos jovens?

lines.speaker: Seu Antônio
lines.en: They have opportunities I never dreamed of. My granddaughter, working from home, talks to people in five countries a day! Having said that, I think they're more anxious than we were.
lines.pt: Eles têm oportunidades com que eu nunca sonhei. Minha neta, trabalhando de casa, fala com pessoas de cinco países por dia! Dito isso, acho que eles são mais ansiosos do que nós éramos.

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.en: Why do you think that is?
lines.pt: Por que o senhor acha isso?

lines.speaker: Seu Antônio
lines.en: Too much information, too many choices. Given the choice between a phone and a good conversation, I'd choose the conversation every time.
lines.pt: Informação demais, escolhas demais. Entre um celular e uma boa conversa, eu escolheria a conversa sempre.

listening.title: Brazil is getting older
listening.context_pt: Uma demógrafa explica, num podcast, o envelhecimento da população brasileira.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.en: Brazil is undergoing one of the fastest demographic transitions in the world. Having had one of the youngest populations in the 1970s, the country is now ageing rapidly. Two trends explain this. First, the birth rate has fallen dramatically: Brazilian women today have, on average, fewer than two children, compared with around six in the 1960s. Second, life expectancy has increased considerably, thanks to better healthcare and sanitation. The result is a population growing older faster than in many European countries, which took much longer to go through the same change. Faced with this situation, the country will need to rethink its pension system, its healthcare services and even the way its cities are designed. Having said that, an older population also brings opportunities, from new businesses to a more experienced workforce.

questions.q: What was Brazil's population like in the 1970s?
questions.answer: One of the youngest in the world.

questions.q: How many children did Brazilian women have on average in the 1960s, and how many now?
questions.answer: Around six then; fewer than two now.

questions.q: Why has life expectancy increased?
questions.answer: Better healthcare and sanitation.

questions.q: What will the country need to rethink?
questions.answer: Its pension system, healthcare services and city design.

reading.title: The remote work revolution
reading.text: Before 2020, remote work was a privilege enjoyed by a small minority of workers. Then, almost overnight, the COVID-19 pandemic forced millions of office employees to work from their kitchens and living rooms. Having been told for years that remote work was impossible, many companies discovered that it worked surprisingly well. Freed from long commutes, employees gained hours of free time each week. Some left expensive capital cities altogether, moving to smaller towns or the coast and taking their salaries with them. Several countries, including Portugal and Costa Rica, began offering special visas designed to attract "digital nomads". Not everyone has benefited equally, however. Jobs requiring physical presence — in hospitals, shops, factories and construction — cannot be done from home, which means that remote work has, in some ways, increased the gap between different groups of workers. Managers, too, have expressed concerns, arguing that teams working only online lose creativity and that young employees miss out on learning from experienced colleagues. Having experimented with every possible model, many organizations have now settled on a hybrid approach. Having said that, the debate is far from over.

questions.q: What did many companies discover during the pandemic?
questions.answer: That remote work worked surprisingly well.

questions.q: What did some employees do, freed from commuting?
questions.answer: They moved to smaller towns or the coast.

questions.q: Why has remote work increased the gap between workers?
questions.answer: Jobs requiring physical presence can't be done from home.

questions.q: What model have many organizations settled on?
questions.answer: A hybrid approach.

writing.model:
How my generation is different

Born in the early 1990s, my parents' generation grew up in a very different Brazil. Having lived through years of high inflation, they learned to save every penny and to value job security above everything else. My father, having worked for the same company for 32 years, still finds it strange that I've had four jobs in eight years.

My generation, raised with the internet, sees the world differently. Connected to people all over the planet, we tend to be more open to new ideas, cultures and ways of living. Many of my friends, not wanting to spend three hours a day in traffic, have chosen jobs that allow them to work remotely. Others, inspired by influencers and entrepreneurs, have started their own businesses.

We also talk more openly about topics that our parents rarely mentioned, such as mental health, gender equality and the environment. Asked about therapy, my mother once told me that "in my time, we just got on with life". My friends, on the other hand, see therapy as something completely normal.

Having said that, our generation has its own problems. Faced with high rents and unstable jobs, many of us still live with our parents well into our thirties. And, having grown up with smartphones, we often find it difficult to switch off.

In the end, every generation is shaped by the world in which it grows up. Perhaps the most important thing is to keep listening to each other.

grammar.title: Contrast and concession linkers
grammar.explanation_pt:
**1. Although / Even though / Though + oração** (sujeito + verbo)
- "**Although** the city is rich, many people live in poverty."
- **Even though** = mais enfático ("mesmo que, ainda que"): "**Even though** he earns a lot, he never saves."
- **Though** = mais informal; também no fim da frase: "It's expensive. I love it, **though**."

**2. Despite / In spite of + substantivo ou -ing** (sem sujeito + verbo!)
- "**Despite** the rain, we went out." / "**In spite of** being tired, she kept working."
- Para usar uma oração: **despite the fact that** + oração: "**Despite the fact that** it was raining, we went out."
- ⚠️ ❌ "despite **of**" — não existe. ❌ "Despite it was raining".

**3. Whereas / While** → **contraste direto** entre duas coisas (comparação):
- "Rich families have fast internet at home, **whereas** many poor families rely on mobile data."
- "**While** some see AI as a threat, others see it as an opportunity."

**4. However / Nevertheless / On the other hand** → ligam **duas frases** (vêm depois de ponto ou ponto e vírgula, seguidos de vírgula):
- "The internet has created opportunities. **However**, not everyone can access them."
- **Nevertheless / Nonetheless** (formal) = "mesmo assim": "The project was expensive. **Nevertheless**, it was a success."
- **On the other hand** → apresenta o outro lado de um argumento: "On the one hand, ... **On the other hand**, ..."
- **Yet** (formal, = but): "simple **yet** effective"

⚠️ **However não liga duas orações com vírgula** como "but": ❌ "It's cheap, however it's bad." ✅ "It's cheap. However, it's bad." / "It's cheap; however, it's bad."

rows: Although it was late, we kept talking.
Despite the cost, they bought it.
Despite the fact that it was late, we kept talking.
She's tall, whereas her brother is short.
It's fast. On the other hand, it's expensive.

grammar.tip_pt: Truque para não errar: **although** = embora (+ frase completa) · **despite** = apesar de (+ substantivo/-ing). Se em português você diria "apesar **de que**", use **although** ou **despite the fact that**.

listening.title: The digital divide
listening.context_pt: Uma pesquisadora fala sobre a exclusão digital no Brasil.

lines.speaker: Researcher
lines.en: When people hear that most Brazilians are now online, they often assume the digital divide has disappeared. However, the reality is more complex. Although the majority of the population uses the internet, many low-income users rely only on a mobile phone with a limited data plan, whereas wealthier families usually have fast broadband and several devices at home. This difference matters. Doing homework, applying for a job or taking an online course on a small phone screen is much harder. During the pandemic, when classes moved online, many children were left behind despite their schools' efforts. Nevertheless, there is some good news: public Wi-Fi programmes and community centres are helping to narrow the gap. Connection is no longer the only issue, though. Digital skills are just as important.

reading.title: Will AI make us more equal?
reading.text: Artificial intelligence has been described as the most important technology of our time. Yet economists disagree sharply about whether it will reduce or increase inequality. On the one hand, optimists argue that AI tools could empower people who have traditionally been left behind. A small farmer can now get advice about crops in her own language, while a student without access to private tutors can ask a chatbot to explain a difficult maths problem. Although these tools are not perfect, they are often free or cheap. On the other hand, pessimists point out that previous waves of technology tended to benefit those who already had capital and education. Despite creating new jobs, automation has often replaced routine tasks performed by lower-paid workers, whereas highly skilled professionals have seen their productivity — and salaries — increase. There is also the question of who owns the technology: a handful of large companies, most of which are based in the United States and China. In spite of these concerns, most experts agree on one point: the outcome is not inevitable. Whether AI narrows or widens the gap will depend largely on political choices, including investment in education, regulation and public access to digital tools.

writing.model:
Has technology reduced inequality?

On the one hand, technology has opened doors for millions of people. Although many Brazilians still cannot afford a computer, most now have a smartphone, which gives them access to free courses, banking apps and job opportunities. Instant payment systems, for instance, have made it much easier for small businesses and informal workers to receive money, whereas in the past many of them had no bank account at all. Despite its limitations, a phone with an internet connection can be a powerful tool for learning and earning.

On the other hand, technology has also created new forms of inequality. While wealthy families have fast broadband and several devices, many poor families share one phone with a limited data plan. During the pandemic, this difference meant that some children kept learning, whereas others were left behind. Furthermore, automation is replacing routine jobs, yet the new jobs being created usually require skills that low-income workers have had little opportunity to develop.

In my opinion, technology itself is neither good nor bad; it is a double-edged sword. It has certainly reduced some inequalities. Nevertheless, without public investment in internet access and digital education, it may end up widening the gap rather than narrowing it.

grammar.title: Essay structure and formal linkers
grammar.explanation_pt:
**Estrutura clássica (4 parágrafos):**

**1. Introdução** — apresente o tema com uma frase geral e mostre do que o texto vai tratar. Não dê sua opinião completa ainda (ou dê de forma breve, se a pergunta pedir).
"It is often said that university should be free for everyone. This essay will examine both sides of this question."

**2. Parágrafo 1** — **topic sentence** + argumento + exemplo/explicação.
"**Firstly**, free education would increase social mobility. **For instance**, ..."

**3. Parágrafo 2** — outro argumento **ou** o lado oposto.
"**On the other hand**, it could be argued that... **As a result**, ..."

**4. Conclusão** — resuma e dê sua opinião clara. Não traga ideias novas.
"**In conclusion**, **all things considered**, I believe that..."

**Linking words por função:**
- **Adicionar:** furthermore, moreover, in addition, what is more, not only... but also
- **Exemplificar:** for example, for instance, such as, a good example of this is
- **Causa:** because of, due to, owing to, since, as
- **Efeito:** as a result, consequently, therefore, thus, which means that
- **Contraste:** however, nevertheless, on the other hand, although, despite
- **Opinião:** in my view, from my point of view, I firmly believe that, it seems to me that
- **Concluir:** in conclusion, to sum up, all things considered, overall

**Linguagem impessoal** (soa acadêmica e objetiva):
- **It is often argued / claimed / believed that...**
- **There is no doubt that...** / **It is undeniable that...**
- Evite contrações (don't → do not), gírias e frases muito curtas em sequência.

**Dica de ouro:** **não exagere** nos conectores! Um por frase, no máximo — e use variedade.

rows: Furthermore, Moreover, In addition, What is more
For instance, For example, such as
due to, owing to, because of, since
However, On the other hand, Nevertheless
In conclusion, To sum up, All things considered

lines.en: OK. What about the main paragraphs?

listening.title: How examiners mark your essay
listening.context_pt: Uma examinadora explica os critérios de correção de redação em provas de nível B2.

lines.speaker: Examiner
lines.en: Many students think the most important thing in an essay is grammar. In fact, in the Cambridge B2 First, your writing is assessed on four criteria. First, content: have you answered the question and included all the required points? Second, communicative achievement: is the style appropriate — formal, in the case of an essay — and does your text hold the reader's attention? Third, organization: are your ideas logically connected, with clear paragraphs and a good variety of linking words? And finally, language: how wide and accurate is your vocabulary and grammar? So, as you can see, grammar is only one part. A text with a few small mistakes but excellent organization will often score better than a perfect text that doesn't answer the question. My advice? Spend five minutes planning before you write. It makes a huge difference.

questions.q: How many criteria are used to assess writing in B2 First?
questions.answer: Four.

questions.q: What does "content" mean?
questions.answer: Answering the question and including all required points.

questions.q: What does "organization" include?
questions.answer: Logical connection, clear paragraphs and varied linking words.

questions.q: What is the examiner's advice?

reading.title: Model essay: Should university education be free?
reading.text:
In many countries, including Brazil, the cost of higher education is a controversial issue. While public universities offer free courses, places are limited and highly competitive. This essay will consider whether university education should be free for everyone.

There are strong arguments in favour of free higher education. Firstly, it can increase social mobility. When students do not have to pay fees, talented young people from low-income families have a real chance of entering professions such as medicine or engineering. Furthermore, a more educated population tends to benefit the whole economy, as graduates generally earn more and contribute more in taxes.

On the other hand, it could be argued that free education is not truly free, since it is paid for by all taxpayers, including those who never go to university. In addition, if universities receive too little funding, the quality of teaching may suffer. As a result, some experts suggest alternatives, such as income-based loans, where graduates repay their fees only when they earn above a certain salary.

In conclusion, all things considered, I believe that higher education should remain free at public universities, as it is one of the most effective ways of reducing inequality. However, governments must ensure that it is adequately funded and that access is fair for students from all backgrounds.

questions.q: What does the introduction do?
questions.answer: Introduces the topic and says what the essay will consider.

questions.q: What are the two arguments in favour?
questions.answer: It increases social mobility and benefits the economy.

questions.q: What alternative do some experts suggest?
questions.answer: Income-based loans, repaid only above a certain salary.

questions.q: What is the writer's final opinion?
questions.answer: Public university education should remain free but be adequately funded and fair.

writing.task: Write a B2 First–style essay (140–190 words) answering this question: "Some people think that all students should learn to code at school. Do you agree?" Write about 1) future jobs, 2) creativity and problem-solving, and 3) your own idea. Use a clear 4-paragraph structure and formal linkers.
writing.task_pt: Escreva uma redação no estilo B2 First (140–190 palavras) respondendo: "Algumas pessoas acham que todos os alunos deveriam aprender programação na escola. Você concorda?" Escreva sobre 1) empregos do futuro, 2) criatividade e resolução de problemas e 3) uma ideia sua. Use estrutura de 4 parágrafos e conectores formais.
writing.model:
Should all students learn to code at school?

Technology plays a central role in almost every area of modern life. As a result, many people believe that coding should be a compulsory subject at school. This essay will consider whether this is a good idea.

Firstly, digital skills are increasingly valued in the job market. Even professions that are not directly related to technology, such as marketing or medicine, now require people who understand how software works. Furthermore, learning to code develops problem-solving skills, as students must break complex problems into smaller steps and test different solutions.

On the other hand, it could be argued that the school timetable is already full. If coding is added, other important subjects, such as art or physical education, may be reduced. In addition, many schools lack computers and trained teachers.

In conclusion, I believe that all students should have the opportunity to learn basic coding. However, it should be introduced gradually and combined with other subjects rather than replacing them.

culture_note.title: Redação do ENEM x Essay
culture_note.text_pt: Na **redação do ENEM**, o texto é dissertativo-argumentativo e termina com uma **proposta de intervenção**. No **essay** em inglês (Cambridge, IELTS, universidades), o foco é **argumentar com clareza e equilíbrio**, e o limite de palavras é rígido. Os textos em inglês também costumam ser mais **diretos**: frases mais curtas e uma ideia por parágrafo.

summary_pt: Topic sentence no início de cada parágrafo.
Varie conectores: furthermore, for instance, as a result, however, in conclusion.
Formal: sem contrações, linguagem impessoal (It could be argued that...).
